Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G1909 and G153; not ashamed, i.e. irreprehensible: --that needeth not to be ashamed.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells Timothy to study to show himself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. The word describes the workman who has nothing to be ashamed of, because his work stands inspection.
TheologicalSignificance: A single word for an unashamed workman holds no doctrine of its own; its charge is Paul's, that handling God's word rightly is the work that leaves a man with nothing to hide.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
